data.body:
**The example this ticket was filed against is being removed, which changes how the gap must be proven.**

`docker-compose.langfuse.yml:113` was the concrete instance of an unguarded Compose `image:` key — `docker.io/minio/minio:latest`. It is being replaced with a pinned `quay.io/minio/minio:RELEASE.2025-09-07T16-13-09Z` under `stoppable-sorry-budgie` (6d98-28f4), because the Docker Hub repository no longer exists at all: the Hub API returns 404 `object not found` and a token-authed manifest request returns 401, which is what turned the scheduled `Live External Integration` run red.

That fix is unrelated to this gate and does not close it. It does mean a reviewer checking this ticket after 6d98 lands will find no floating tag in the tree and may read the gap as already fixed. It is not: `scripts/check_uv_pin.py:400` still globs `**/Dockerfile*` only, so no Compose `image:` key is guarded, and nothing prevents the next floating tag from being added.

**Consequence for this ticket's tests.** A regression test can no longer point at a live offender, so it needs a fixture Compose file with a deliberately floating tag and an assertion that the checker rejects it. That is the more durable shape anyway — a test that depends on a real file's staying broken would have started failing the moment 6d98 landed.

Worth noting that the repository was one `docker compose pull` away from this being invisible: every other image in that file — langfuse, clickhouse, redis, postgres — is pinned, so the single unpinned key was the outlier the guard was supposed to catch and structurally could not.

Cross-reference: `docs/experiments/code-review-threshold-calibration-code-v5.md:107-110` cites this exact pair as its worked example of "a guard that exists but cannot fail". It is a dated experiment record, so it is deliberately left unedited and now describes a state the tree has moved past.
